sasha (platform): heads up — I'm proposing we split fncall/structured-output telemetry into two separate sampling streams: strict_rejects (100%) and soft_fails (sampled). rationale: strict rejects drive user-facing rollbacks and billing disputes; soft fails are noisy and currently drown dashboards.
li (eng-telemetry): makes sense. can you sketch what fields we'd keep for strict_rejects vs soft_fails?
sasha (platform): strict_rejects = {route_id, model_variant, schema_id, reject_code, user_route_tags, request_id} — everything needed for repro and billing. soft_fails = {route_id, schema_id, score, snippet_hash, sample_flag} — smaller, maybe 1-5% global.
noah (product): Q: how will this affect the console UX? product wants to show a per-route reject rate and also examples for QA.
sasha (platform): plan: dashboard shows two lines: strict_reject_rate (live, high fidelity) and soft_fail_rate (smoothed, sampled). example listing will only show strict rejects + sampled soft_fail examples (with redaction).
maya (privacy): important — any example text must be redacted client-side before it lands in telemetry. we should add a privacy-step in pipeline: redact PII, strip long user content, and only include a hash for debugging when needed.
li (eng-telemetry): implementation note: we can create two Kafka topics: fncall.strict.rejects (no sampling) and fncall.soft.fail.sampled (ingest sampler). tagging will be fncall:type=strict|soft and fncall:sample_rate. dashboards query against materialized metrics.
sasha (platform): agreed. also adding a new metric name convention: fncall.rejects.rate (labels: route, schema, variant, reject_code) and fncall.softfail.examples.count (sampled).
noah (product): about rollouts — we should canary sampling config for 48h on 10% of routes, measure signal-to-noise. fallback: if strict_reject_count changes >5% after split, pause rollout.
li (eng-telemetry): suggest we add a histogram for time-to-detect (from first strict reject to alert firing) so we don't regress alert latency.
sasha (platform): good call. ops-bot: can you create an alert stub: "fncall.strict.rejects.rate > X for 5m" and link the new SLO doc?
ops-bot: created alert #PLAT-3123 (draft). preview: Metric fncall.rejects.rate by route, threshold 0.5% sustained for 5m.
maya (privacy): one more: examples in UI must have an "origin" tag — customer-generated vs system-synth. system-synth examples ok to show; customer-generated must be redacted and require customer opt-in.
sasha (platform): we'll add origin and a redaction flag to the strict payload. default UI will hide text until redaction verified.
li (eng-telemetry): telemetry storage cost question — strict stream will increase costs. propose tagging strict events with billing_tag=reject_forensics, which can be subject to retention TTL (90 days). soft samples TTL 30 days.
noah (product): spinner Q: will customers be billed for strict_reject analysis events? we should avoid surprise charges. product suggests keeping forensic telemetry off by default for free-tier accounts and on for enterprise or opt-in.
sasha (platform): agreed — plan: telemetry collection is internal-only; if a customer requests per-request forensic logs for debugging, we gate via console toggle and generate an on-demand export (audit path) which may be billed. default: platform stores rejects for 90 days under internal billing bucket.
li (eng-telemetry): rollout steps I propose: 1) infra: new topics + sampler config 2) API: instrument fncall path to emit strict vs soft tags 3) storage: materialized metrics + retention policies 4) dashboard: add split chart + examples panel 5) canary: 10% routes, 48h 6) ship. estimate 2 sprints.
sasha (platform): timeline ok. need eng-security review for redaction and retention. maya?
maya (privacy): i'll run the redaction checklist and provide approved regexes / transforms. one requirement: do not log raw user-provided auth tokens even in forensic payloads.
li (eng-telemetry): small implementation question — how do we detect strict vs soft? current validator returns a code set: VALID, SOFT_FAIL, STRICT_FAIL. we'll map STRICT_FAIL -> strict, others -> soft. fine?
sasha (platform): yes. but add a post-validator hook: if a SOFT_FAIL has high confidence score < 0.2, treat as strict for alerting. avoids stealth breakages.
noah (product): can we add an annotation in the dashboard for schema changes and deployment versions? we had confusion last time where many soft fails coincided with a model variant deploy.
sasha (platform): will add deployment tags (deploy_id, git_sha) to strict events. UI will surface last 24h deploys overlay.
li (eng-telemetry): final note on sampling entropy: use deterministic sampling keyed by route_id + day so examples are reproducible for debugging.
sasha (platform): sounds good. next actions: li to open infra PR, maya to post redaction rules, ops-bot to create alert + canary ticket, product to write user-facing console copy for forensic toggle. I'll draft the rollout doc and share.
noah (product): thanks — this clarifies. small follow-up: can we show estimated cost delta on the rollout page? ops-bot / finance may help.
ops-bot: Created ticket #PLAT-3124: "fncall-telemetry-cost-estimate" assigned to finance-ops.
sasha (platform): perfect. I'll post the rollout doc in #eng-platform tomorrow.
li (eng-telemetry): one last quick code snippet for the sampler config (pseudo):
```
topic: fncall.soft.fail.sampled
sample_key: hash(route_id || day)
sample_rate: 0.02
retain_ttl_days: 30
```
sasha (platform): nice. leaving this here for the write-up. thanks all :thumbsup:
